e.etymology: A modern American name in the family of Jaylen, Waylon and Dylan, also spelled Daylen and Daylon.
A form of Janelle with a -y ending, favored by Hispanic families in the US, where it is also written Janely and Yanely. Janelle is an elaboration of Jane.
An English surname from Middle English lyon, lion, a nickname for a brave or fierce man or a name taken from an inn sign. It is also the name of the French city of Lyon.

e.meaning: a labyrinth, a puzzle of winding paths
e.etymology: The English word for a labyrinth, used as a name in the 2020s, and a short form of Mazikeen, the demon called Maze in the series Lucifer. Maze is separately an English and French surname.

assoc.t: Mazikeen, called Maze, the demon in the series Lucifer

e.etymology: An English surname taken from the village of Eldon in County Durham, Old English for Ella's hill. It was a steady American boys' name in the early 1900s.
A phonetic American spelling of Desiree, from French Désirée, desired, which goes back to the Latin name Desiderata.
A short form of Breanna and a spelling of Bria, both from the Brian family of names. Brea is also a Galician surname and the Spanish word for tar.

assoc.t: La Brea Tar Pits in Los Angeles
Brea, a city in Orange County, California

e.note: Brea is Spanish for tar, as in the La Brea Tar Pits.

e.etymology: From Greek Arion, the name of a 7th-century BC poet said to have been carried to shore by a dolphin, and of a swift immortal horse in Greek myth.
The Italian and Portuguese form of Adrian, from Latin Hadrianus, a man from Hadria, the town that also named the Adriatic Sea. The emperor Hadrian made the name famous.
Built on Ana, the Spanish form of Anna, with a -ly ending; close to Analí and to Analía, the Spanish blend of Ana and Lía.
e.note: The spelling looks close to the English word anally, which can draw teasing.

e.etymology: From Arabic na'im, bliss, ease or comfort. The Quran uses the word for the delights of paradise, as in the Gardens of Bliss.
From Hawaiian ke, the, and koa, which means both warrior and the koa tree. It is also a short form of longer Hawaiian names beginning with Kekoa-.
A modern blend of Cali with the -ana ending of Eliana and Juliana.
A respelling of Daxton, an American coinage of the 2000s that adds the surname ending -ton to Dax, in the pattern of Paxton and Braxton.
A modern American coinage in the pattern of Zyaire and Kyaire, with an Ny- opening.
The English word riven, split or torn apart, from Old Norse rifa, to tear. As a name it follows River and Raven, helped by characters in League of Legends and Fate: The Winx Saga.

assoc.t: Riven, the exiled swordswoman in League of Legends
Riven, a specialist in Winx Club and Fate: The Winx Saga
Riven, the 1997 sequel to the computer game Myst

e.etymology: A spelling of the word choice used as a name. Choyce is also an old English surname, a variant of Joyce.
A Scottish clan surname from Old Norse logmadr, lawman, by way of Gaelic. It peaked as an American first name in the 1970s, when Lamont Sanford was a lead character on Sanford and Son.
namesakes: Lamont Sanford (the son on Sanford and Son)
Lamont Cranston (alter ego of the pulp hero The Shadow)

e.etymology: A spelling of Marcel, from Latin Marcellus, a pet form of Marcus, the Roman name tied to the god Mars. Marcell is also the standard Hungarian form.
A Welsh surname from ap Rhys, son of Rhys, a name meaning ardor. It has been used as a first name in the US since the 1800s.

assoc.t: price, the everyday word for what something costs

e.etymology: A spelling of Lily, the flower name, and in German, French and Hungarian a pet form of Elisabeth, as in the wartime song Lili Marleen. In Basque, lili means flower.
namesakes: Lili Reinhart (actress who played Betty on Riverdale)
Lili Taylor (actress in Mystic Pizza and Six Feet Under)

e.etymology: In the US mostly a blend of the Ka- prefix with Mya, in the pattern of Amya and Jamya. Kamya is also an Indian name from Sanskrit kamya, desirable.
From an English surname for someone who lived near a cliff, Old English clif. It spread as a first name in honor of Robert Clive, the 18th-century general known as Clive of India.
namesakes: Clive Owen (English actor in Children of Men)
Clive Davis (record executive who signed Whitney Houston)
C. S. Lewis (author of the Narnia books, born Clive Staples Lewis)

e.etymology: From Greek xenia, hospitality, the duty of host to guest, from xenos, stranger. Saint Xenia, a 5th-century nun, and Saint Xenia of St. Petersburg made it a favorite in the Orthodox world.
namesakes: Xenia Onatopp (the villain in the Bond film GoldenEye)

assoc.t: Xenia, Ohio, city struck by a major 1974 tornado

e.etymology: From Arabic aman, safety and peace, borrowed into Persian, Urdu, Hindi and Punjabi. In India it is used by Hindu, Sikh and Muslim families alike.

assoc.t: Aman, luxury resort and hotel group

e.etymology: A modern American spelling of Kia or Kiya, in step with Kiara and Kiana.

assoc.t: Kia, the Korean car maker (same sound as KEE-uh)

e.etymology: An Arabic form of Joseph, from Hebrew Yosef, he will add. Yusuf is a prophet in Islam, and the twelfth chapter of the Quran tells his story.
From Sanskrit advaita, not two, the term for the non-dualist school of Hindu philosophy, which holds the self and ultimate reality to be one. The -th spelling is typical of South India.
A pet form of Zissel or Zisse, from Yiddish zis, sweet. It is used almost entirely in Hasidic and other Orthodox Jewish communities.
e.note: Sounds close to the English word sissy, which could draw teasing where the name is unfamiliar.
